text: About 2.1 million years ago, the land where Yellowstone sits tore open.
The Huckleberry Ridge eruption threw out roughly 2,400 cubic kilometers of rock and ash.
That's enough to bury the whole state of Rhode Island nearly half a mile deep.
Its ash has been found as far away as seafloor cores off California,
part of a single ash layer traced across about 3,000 kilometers.
